title: Rhombus Botnet Investigation
description: Investigate and respond to a Rhombus Linux DDoS botnet infection affecting your network. The botnet targets VPS and IoT devices, communicates with C2 servers, and performs DDoS attacks.
prerequisites: Familiarity with network services and security tools
outcomes: Identify and investigate suspicious services and network connections

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: You are a cybersecurity analyst tasked with investigating a Rhombus Linux DDoS botnet infection affecting your network. The Rhombus botnet targets VPS and IoT devices, communicates with command-and-control (C2) servers, and performs distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks. Your goal is to identify, contain, and mitigate the botnet activities.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the sandbox in cloud using the following credentials: To begin, enter the word 'start' to progress to the next level.
levels.local_content: Access the local sandbox using the following credentials: To begin, enter the word 'start' to progress to the next level.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Beacon Service
levels.content: Investigate the system services on bot1 and identify the suspicious beacon service used by the Rhombus botnet. The flag is the name of the timer service.
levels.solution: Look for services related to system health or updates that might be unusual.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: The beacon service is likely disguised as a legitimate system service.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Check the list of system timers for any unusual services.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Use the command 'systemctl list-timers' to find the suspicious service.

levels.title: Identify C2 Communication
levels.content: Analyze network connections from bot1 to identify the command-and-control (C2) server communication. Determine the IP address and port used for this communication. The flag is the port number.
levels.solution: Check active network connections and listen ports.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: The C2 communication is likely using a non-standard port.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Look for active network connections and listening ports.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Use the command 'ss -tulnp' to find the C2 communication port.

levels.title: Contain C2 Communication
levels.content: Implement measures to contain the C2 communication. Block the identified port on bot1 to prevent further communication with the C2 server. The flag is the port number you block.
levels.solution: Use firewall rules to block the specific port.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Blocking the C2 communication port will prevent the botnet from receiving commands.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use firewall rules to block the specific port.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Use the command 'iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 2222 -j DROP' to block the port.
